text: Job Description Overview AtkinsRéalis Global Technology Centre (GTC) Canada Business is looking to appoint a number of Highways BIM Designer’s to support the delivery of complex civil engineering and multidisciplinary designs across a range of major projects. Drawing upon a diverse skill set and a proven track record of delivery, AtkinsRéalis GTC’s Canada business is playing an integral role in some of the most challenging and exciting engineering projects in the Transportation realm. We pride ourselves in offering a truly multi-disciplinary capability and bring exciting opportunities to influence major projects from beginning to end. Our vision is to be the world’s best Infrastructure Consultancy by leveraging BIM and embracing the digital future to bring about transformational benefits for the Transportation Engineering industry. This key post will be based out of Bangalore where we have thriving AtkinsRéalis office, which deliver to all AtkinsRéalis regions across the world. Our portfolio of work continues to grow, and we will offer a challenging and rewarding opportunity to apply knowledge, experience, and problem-solving skills. Your Role Responsibilities Produce AutoCAD and MicroStation 2D drawings and other deliverables. Actively contribute to project design development by contributing to internal coordination. Produce all types of Highways discipline 2D Drawings and other deliverables. Perform self-assurance of all Highways discipline drawing and model deliverables. Provide quality control for compliance to company/project standards of deliverables. Maintain a high level of competency of all BIM software tools used at AtkinsRéalis. About You Requirements A Bachelor’s degree or Diploma holder in Civil Engineering with minimum of 4 to 6 years of industry experience, preferably in the Highways Domain. Must be an advanced user or expert user in Autodesk AutoCAD, Civil3D, and Bentley MicroStation with a minimum of 2 to 3 years. AutoCAD experience must, detailed understanding of the CAD user interface and all its features to perform. MicroStation experience must, detailed understanding of the MicroStation user interface and all its features to perform. Technical proficiency in the use of the latest common CDE systems: Bentley ProjectWise and Autodesk Vault. Must be well versed in best practices for use of Autodesk AutoCAD, and Bentley MicroStation and other industry standard BIM platforms. Track record in BIM design and coordination including multidisciplinary projects and ideally demonstrable experience within a Civil Engineering Design environment particularly the Highways domain. Technical awareness/knowledge of engineering design issues including awareness of health and safety risks. Qualifications and attributes Excellent time management skills. Experience of using written and spoken English within a business environment. A Bachelor’s degree or Diploma holder in Civil Engineering with minimum of 4 to 5 years of industry experience, preferably in the Highways Domain. Constantly striving towards continuous improvement and innovation. Flexible and engaging with resilience, drive and self-motivation Ability to exercise initiative and take ownership of project issues Ability to collaborate successfully within a project and team environment but also to work independently and in a client environment Ability to adapt to different cultures and working environments to build rapport with customers Highly IT literate, excellent command of standard office software, knowledge of IT infrastructure and hardware. Rewards & Benefits Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career. Enjoy competitive salaries, employee rewards and a brilliant range of benefits you can tailor to suit your own health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle choices. Make the most of a myriad of opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise. And combine our hybrid working culture and flexible holiday allowances to balance a great job and fulfilling personal life .
